query: Earlier empirical-potential and first-principles studies primarily targeted phase-transition temperature, while other fusion properties remain difficult because they require free energies on both sides of the transition with vibrational entropy, anharmonicity, and electron–vibration coupling retained. Explicit ab initio free-energy evaluation is highly accurate but depends on costly molecular dynamics. TOR-TILD increased throughput for elemental and binary systems, yet slows substantially for multicomponent high-entropy systems. Under the constraint that the free energies of both solid and fluid states and the relevant entropy terms remain faithful, what single testable methodological hypothesis could substantially reduce the cost of obtaining fusion and high-temperature thermodynamic properties? State the proposed intervention and why it should work, predict its speed and fidelity relative to explicit ab initio molecular-dynamics workflows and TOR-TILD, define composition and temperature boundaries, cite supporting evidence from prior elemental or binary results, and specify a decisive benchmark of phase free energies and derived observables that would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: A unified 'ML-sampled, DFT-reweighted thermodynamic integration' workflow—using temperature-aware machine-learning (ML) potentials to sample anharmonic solids and liquids, compute absolute free energies via thermodynamic integration to reference states, and then apply ab initio free-energy perturbation/reweighting (with Mermin-DFT electronic free energies per frame) to correct to DFT—can reduce the cost of obtaining fusion and high-temperature thermodynamic properties by at least an order of magnitude relative to explicit ab initio molecular-dynamics (AIMD) free-energy workflows, while maintaining fidelity of solid and liquid free energies (including vibrational entropy, anharmonicity, and electron–vibration coupling) within near-AIMD accuracy for multicomponent metallic and simple ionic systems near melting.
generation.material_initial_state: Multicomponent metallic alloy or simple ionic compound in both solid and liquid states near the melting region (e.g., equiatomic quaternary/quinary high-entropy alloys; 200–1000 atom supercells assembled at target compositions).
generation.intervention: Replace explicit AIMD-based free-energy evaluation with a two-stage approach: (1) active-learning training of a temperature-aware ML interatomic potential (e.g., message-passing neural network) on a compact set of Mermin-DFT configurations spanning solid and liquid environments and target composition; (2) perform long ML molecular dynamics in both phases to sample anharmonic configurations; compute absolute free energies using thermodynamic integration (TI) to an Einstein crystal (solid) and to an ideal-gas or soft-sphere reference (liquid) under the ML Hamiltonian; (3) correct ML free energies to DFT via multi-histogram/MBAR free-energy perturbation using ab initio single-point electronic free energies (Mermin-DFT, finite electronic temperature) evaluated on subsampled ML configurations.
generation.conditions: DFT: generalized-gradient or meta-GGA functional with Mermin smearing at the target electronic temperature; supercell sizes ≥200 atoms; k-point sampling appropriate for large cells (Γ-only or sparse mesh); ML: active learning to ensure phase-space overlap, trained on 10^3–10^4 diverse frames covering solid and liquid; MD lengths ≥100 ps per phase; TI paths: smooth coupling parameter with ≥8–12 λ points; reweighting: MBAR/Zwanzig perturbation with ≥10^3 ab initio single-point evaluations per phase and temperature; temperatures spanning ~0.6–1.2×Tm; pressures near ambient unless otherwise specified.
generation.structural_mediator: Accurate phase-space sampling of both solid and liquid nuclear configurations by the ML potential, ensuring strong overlap with the ab initio distribution so that reweighting (free-energy perturbation/MBAR) is statistically stable. For solids, temperature-dependent effective potential behavior emerges naturally from ML sampling; for liquids, local coordination and short-range order distributions are faithfully reproduced.
generation.mechanism: Anharmonic vibrational entropy is retained by ML MD sampling along the TI path for both phases. The ab initio correction transfers the ML-sampled free energy to the DFT Hamiltonian via free-energy perturbation, provided configuration-space overlap is sufficient. Electronic entropy and electron–vibration coupling are incorporated by evaluating the electronic free energy (Mermin DFT, including -T S_el) on each sampled configuration used for reweighting; the dependence of electronic free energy on instantaneous nuclear structure captures electron–vibration coupling within the adiabatic, finite-T electronic framework. This avoids costly AIMD forces while preserving ab initio fidelity of the thermodynamics.
generation.predicted_outcome: Relative to explicit AIMD free-energy workflows, total wall-clock cost to obtain solid and liquid free energies, melting point, latent heat, and high-T heat capacities will drop by ~10×–50× for multicomponent alloys and compounds, with accuracy comparable to AIMD: phase free energies within ~5–15 meV/atom near Tm, melting points within ~50–150 K, latent heats within ~5–10%. Compared to TOR-TILD, throughput for quaternary/quinary systems improves by ~3×–8× under similar accuracy, especially when surveying composition space, because the ML sampling amortizes the cost and the DFT correction uses single-point evaluations rather than full dynamics.
generation.baseline: Explicit ab initio molecular-dynamics workflows for absolute free energies (e.g., TI or nested approaches with DFT forces) and the TOR-TILD pipeline for elemental/binary systems.
generation.boundary: Most reliable for metallic and simple ionic systems without strong electronic correlations, magnetic frustration, or non-adiabatic transport dominating near Tm. Compositionally up to quinary high-entropy alloys where local chemical complexity is captured by the ML descriptors and training set. Temperature window ~0.6–1.2×Tm at ambient pressure; at much higher temperatures or deep supercooling, electronic non-adiabatic effects and rare-event sampling may reduce fidelity. Requires demonstrable phase-space overlap (effective sample size ≥10% in MBAR) between ML and DFT ensembles.
generation.uncertainty: Accuracy for electron–vibration coupling in liquids relies on the adiabatic Mermin-DFT treatment; strong non-adiabatic effects or correlated electrons may violate assumptions. If ML potential lacks sufficient coverage of rare liquid configurations (e.g., transient cavitation or local polymorphs), reweighting may become biased. Quantitative speedup depends on ML training efficiency and DFT single-point cost for large supercells; reported ranges may narrow with system-specific tuning.

falsification_experiment.design: Select a multicomponent benchmark (e.g., equiatomic NiCoCrFeMn alloy or a quaternary simple ionic compound). For each material, compute absolute free energies of solid and liquid at 3–4 temperatures bracketing Tm using: (A) explicit AIMD TI or the most accurate ab initio free-energy method available; (B) TOR-TILD where applicable; (C) the proposed ML-sampled, DFT-reweighted TI workflow. Use identical supercell sizes, electronic temperatures, and consistent pseudopotentials. Ensure MBAR/reweighting diagnostics (effective sample size, overlap) are recorded.
measurements: Absolute Helmholtz/Gibbs free energies per atom for solid and liquid at each temperature
Melting temperature Tm (from ΔG(T)=0 or two-phase coexistence check)
Latent heat of fusion and entropy of fusion
Heat capacity above Tm (liquid) and below Tm (solid)
Thermal expansion coefficient and compressibility near Tm
MBAR overlap metrics and effective sample size in reweighting
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: The hypothesis is falsified if any of the following hold: (i) phase free energies from the ML-reweighted workflow deviate from AIMD/TOR-TILD by >20 meV/atom at temperatures near Tm; (ii) predicted Tm differs by >200 K from AIMD/TOR-TILD references; (iii) latent heat or entropy of fusion differ by >15%; (iv) MBAR/reweighting fails (effective sample size <5% or inconsistent bootstrap confidence intervals) for either phase, indicating insufficient ensemble overlap; or (v) systematic bias is observed across all measured temperatures (consistent over/underestimation relative to reference) exceeding stated tolerances.
